questions.text: What is the shell register map (offset, width, reset value and access of every register)?
questions.default: Word offsets 0x00 TICK WO, 0x04 RX_BYTE WO, 0x08 REPLY_LEN RO, 0x0C REPLY_IDX RW, 0x10 REPLY_DATA RO, 0x14 TELE_LEN RO, 0x18 TELE_IDX RW, 0x1C TELE_DATA RO, 0x20 TELE_TAKE WO, 0x24 STATUS RO, all 32 bits and reset 0
questions.reason: The request names these registers but gives no offsets
questions.answer:
IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag
STAT: offset 0x09, RO, reset 0: [0] telemetry on, [1] busy
RIDX: offset 0x03, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
RWORD: offset 0x04, RO, reset 0: bytes 4i..4i+3 of the reply, first byte on top, zero past the end
RLEN: offset 0x02, RO, reset 0: length in bytes of the latest reply, 0 if none
TICK: offset 0x01, WO, reset 0: [7:0] n ticks
TIDX: offset 0x06, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
TWORD: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: same for the telemetry frame
TAKE: offset 0x08, WO, reset 0: any write takes the held telemetry frame
TLEN: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: length of the held telemetry frame, 0 if none
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
unmapped: no register at an offset: reads 0, writes ignored (read-only registers behave the same on write)
questions.evidence: IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag

questions.text: Is the telemetry period in register 6 changed by a start with period 1 to 3, and what does a start with a period of 0 do when the period is still 100?
questions.default: Period 1 to 3 gives 4; zero keeps the current period
questions.answer: Partly. The spec does not put the telemetry period in register 6: offset 6 is TIDX, the held-frame word index (RW, bits [6:0]). The period is set by a TLM_START command, which the spec does not map to a register offset. Within that pacer rule, a start with period 1 to 3 sets the period to 4, and a start with period 0 keeps the current period (100 after reset). Your proposed default matches the spec.
questions.evidence: Pacer: TLM_START restarts the count (period 0 keeps, below 4 raised to 4); a frame falls due every period ticks; one held frame; overruns dropped; STOP forgets the held frame; TAKE releases it.

questions.text: Does a telemetry start restart the tick count to the next due tick, and is the held frame kept?
questions.default: The due counter restarts at zero; a held frame is kept
questions.reason: Request says restarts the count and only stop forgets a frame
questions.answer: Partly specified. TLM_START restarts the count, and the held frame is kept, because only STOP forgets a held frame. The spec does not say the count restarts at zero or what the next due tick is, so the proposed default's 'restarts at zero' is not confirmed.
